One of the forgotten Olympic stories includes the part that referred to art. The original idea behind reviving the ancient Olympic Games included both sports and art. Pierre de Coubertin intended to make it part of the first modern Olympic Games held in Athens in 1896, but the art competitors had to wait for another 16 years, until the 1912 Summer Olympics in Stockholm. The contestants were competing in five categories: architecture, literature, music, painting and sculpture. Creations had to obey two rules: they had to be inspired by sport and they had to be originals (no publishing before the Games).

Artists participated in seven Summer Olympic Games: 1912 in Stockholm, 1920 in Antwerp, 1924 in Paris, 1928 in Amsterdam, 1932 in Los Angeles, 1936 in Berlin and in 1948 in London. The interesting fact is that the first gold medal for literature was awarded to Pierre de Coubertin, a person who initiated the story about modern Olympics that included art. He was awarded for his poem "Ode to Sport".

Due to the rule that only amateurs can participate in the Olympic Games, art competitions were later replaced by non-competitive art and cultural festivals that were held simultaneously with Olympics. Artists’ works were exhibited parallel to every Olympic Games ever since by means of the Cultural Olympiad.
